subject: Career
title: Never Say Yes to the First Offer
description: One-minute skill: Never Say Yes to the First Offer.

hook.text: The offer sounds great. Your instinct says take it. But accepting instantly leaves money on the table.

buildup.text: First offers are rarely final offers. There's almost always a range with room above.

discovery.text: Even a simple 'Is there flexibility?' can unlock 5-15% more without any hardball.

twist.text: Accepting too fast also signals low expectations. It can make the employer wonder if they overpaid.

climax.text: Say: 'I'm excited about this. Let me review the full package and follow up tomorrow.'

punchline.text: Pause. Review. Then respond. Never on the spot.

quiz.question: Why shouldn't you accept the first salary offer immediately?
options: There's usually a range with room above

details.summary: Accepting a first offer forfeits negotiation leverage, since employers nearly always include a negotiation buffer. Pausing to evaluate signals professionalism and gives both sides room to find a mutually beneficial agreement beyond the initial proposal.
details.whyItMatters: Companies budget for negotiation. Accepting the first number instantly leaves that budget unspent and signals you may undervalue your own contributions.
takeaways: Employers expect a counter; saying yes too fast can surprise them
Pausing to evaluate shows confidence and professionalism
Even a modest counter often yields a meaningful improvement

faq.question: What is a polite way to signal I won't accept the first offer immediately?
faq.answer: Thank the employer warmly, express genuine enthusiasm for the role, and request twenty-four to forty-eight hours to review the total package. This buys you time without creating tension or signaling disinterest.

faq.question: Does this advice still apply if the first offer seems very generous?
faq.answer: Yes, because you may lack visibility into the full compensation range. Even generous-looking offers can undervalue your profile. Asking about flexibility in equity, signing bonus, or benefits often reveals additional room.
